landmarks.name: Chichen Itza
landmarks.writeup: A large pre-Columbian archaeological site built by the Maya civilization, famous for the pyramid of Kukulkan.

wiki.extract: Chichen Itza was a large pre-Columbian city built by the Maya people of the Terminal Classic period. The archeological site is located in Tinúm Municipality, Yucatán, Mexico.

landmarks.name: Teotihuacan
landmarks.writeup: An ancient Mesoamerican city known for its massive Pyramids of the Sun and Moon.

wiki.extract: Teotihuacan is an ancient Mesoamerican city located in a sub-valley of the Valley of Mexico, which is located in the State of Mexico, 40 kilometers (25 mi) northeast of modern-day Mexico City.

landmarks.name: Palacio de Bellas Artes
landmarks.writeup: A prominent cultural center in Mexico City known for its architecture and murals.

wiki.extract: The Palacio de Bellas Artes is a prominent cultural center in Mexico City. It hosts performing arts events, literature events and plastic arts galleries and exhibitions. "Bellas Artes" for short, has been called the "art cathedral of Mexico", and is located on the western side of the historic center of Mexico City which is close to the Alameda Central park.

landmarks.name: Copper Canyon
landmarks.writeup: A group of six canyons in the Sierra Madre Occidental, larger and deeper than the Grand Canyon.

wiki.extract: Copper Canyon is a group of six distinct canyons in the Sierra Madre Occidental in the southwestern part of the state of Chihuahua in northwestern Mexico that is 65,000 square kilometres (25,000 sq mi) in size. The canyons were formed by six rivers that drain the western side of the Sierra Tarahumara. All six rivers merge into the Rio Fuerte and empty into the Gulf of California. The walls of the canyon are a copper/green color, which is the origin of the name.

landmarks.name: Frida Kahlo Museum
landmarks.writeup: Also known as La Casa Azul, it is the former home of the famous Mexican artist Frida Kahlo.

wiki.extract: The Frida Kahlo Museum, also known as The Blue House for the structure's cobalt-blue walls, is a historic house museum and art museum dedicated to the life and work of Mexican artist Frida Kahlo. It is in the Colonia del Carmen neighborhood of Coyoacán in Mexico City. The building was Kahlo's birthplace, the home where she grew up, lived with her husband Diego Rivera for a number of years, and where she later died in a room on the upper floor. In 1957, Rivera donated the home and its contents to turn it into a museum in Kahlo's honor.

cultural_events.name: Día de los Muertos
cultural_events.writeup: A traditional festival honoring deceased loved ones with altars, offerings, and celebrations.

cultural_events.name: Guelaguetza
cultural_events.writeup: An indigenous cultural event in Oaxaca featuring traditional dances, music, and costumes.

cultural_events.name: Cinco de Mayo
cultural_events.writeup: Commemorates the Mexican army's victory over French forces at the Battle of Puebla.

cultural_events.name: Semana Santa
cultural_events.writeup: Holy Week celebrations with religious processions and ceremonies across the country.

cultural_events.name: Festival Internacional Cervantino
cultural_events.writeup: An annual arts festival in Guanajuato showcasing music, theater, and dance from around the world.

food_writeup: Mexican cuisine is known for its bold flavors and diverse ingredients, including corn, beans, chili peppers, and avocados. Popular dishes include tacos, mole, tamales, and enchiladas, reflecting a blend of indigenous and Spanish influences.
brief_history: Mexico has a rich history dating back to advanced pre-Columbian civilizations like the Maya and Aztec. It was colonized by Spain in the 16th century and gained independence in 1821. The country has since undergone political and social transformations, becoming a federal republic with a diverse cultural heritage.

important_people.name: Benito Juárez
important_people.description: Former president and national hero known for liberal reforms.

important_people.name: Frida Kahlo
important_people.description: Renowned painter famous for her self-portraits and Mexican identity.

important_people.name: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz

current_conflicts: Mexico faces challenges related to organized crime, drug trafficking, and violence in certain regions, impacting security and governance.
